input.title: Accept more currency symbols and separators in parseAmount
input.body:
File: src/util/money.ts

parseAmount only strips the symbols €$£¥ before validating the amount, so a rupee sign (₹) or a currency-code prefix like "CHF" leaves non-digit characters in the string and the regex rejects it as not a number. Likewise the Swiss thousands separator (') is never stripped, only commas are. Extend the symbol-stripping regex to cover the rupee sign (and ideally any non-breaking/narrow space and apostrophe thousands separators, plus letter currency prefixes such as CHF) so amounts like ₹1,250.00 and CHF 1'200.00 parse correctly.

label: bug
file: src/util/money.ts

parseAmount() only strips the symbols €, $, £ and ¥ before checking the text is a number, so a rupee sign (₹) or a currency-code prefix like "CHF" (and the Swiss apostrophe thousands separator) are left in the string and fail the numeric regex, producing "The amount is not a number". The fix belongs in parseAmount's symbol-stripping step, which needs to cover ₹ and similar cases.
